items.title: Live Tourism Economy: Where Event-Driven Travel Spending Lands
items.summary: A concert or a final now decides where hundreds of thousands of people travel and when. The harder question is who captures the money that arrives with them. The Skift Live Tourism Summit is where destinations and the live industry settle it.

items.title: Brand USA Chief in Advanced Talks to Rejoin NYC Tourism: Scoop
items.summary: The pivot comes two years after Fred Dixon joined the nation's destination marketing organization.

items.title: Can’t Afford Hoxton or Moxy? Generator’s New CEO Says: We’re Premium Too — But Just £40 Per Bunk
items.summary: Strip out the four-star furniture, add bunk beds, charge £40 a night. Now convince your guests they’re staying somewhere premium. That’s Generator’s pitch.

items.title: United Adds 10 Routes Across Europe and Asia — From Okinawa to Ibiza
items.summary: Unique destinations have become a central part of United’s strategy as it caters to more premium travelers and operates in an increasingly competitive transatlantic market.

items.title: Ixigo Tests Packaged Tours for Trains, Uber Becomes a New Distribution Engine
items.summary: Ixigo is taking a smart, low-risk approach to packaged travel. Rather than build and operate its own tours, it is testing demand by putting IRCTC-curated trips on its platform. If travelers bite, packaged tours could become the OTA’s next major product category.

items.title: Three South Korean Carriers Are Merging Into One Low-Cost Giant
items.summary: A supercharged budget airline backed by the flag carrier changes the math for everyone else in a low-cost market that still has too many brands.

items.title: Wall Street Is Starting to Believe Airbnb’s Growth Story
items.summary: The bank's thesis that Airbnb's "Acceleration is here to stay" is a bold statement. The potential is there. Focus and execution will be all-important.

items.title: Cruise Ports Top the Labor Day List and the K-Shaped Travel Gap is Narrowing
items.summary: Airfare and gas prices are up, but research suggests Americans are committed to spending on travel.
